question.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=-\frac{1}{2}$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order,  what is the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ={120}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & 2x & ={240}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our two equations for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{120}^{∘}}{2}+\frac{n\cdot {360}^{∘}}{2} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{{240}^{∘}}{2}+\frac{n\cdot {360}^{∘}}{2} \\ x & ={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={120}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={60}^{∘}$ and $x={120}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={240}^{∘}$ and $x={300}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x={60}^{∘},\,{120}^{∘},\,{240}^{∘},\,{300}^{∘}
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{1}={60}^{∘}$ and ${x}_{3}={240}^{∘},$ the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$ is $60\cdot 240=14\,400.$
